notes: Access: robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (only generic scraper/bad-bot bans); site is a client-rendered Next.js app so plain HTTP fetch returns an empty shell -- used Playwright (tier 2) to render pages and read the DOM/text, per access-tier rules. Discovery: read the fully rendered main-nav mega menu (WOMEN/MEN/HOME/JEWELRY/SAREE/GIFTING/CRAFTS) exhaustively -- no Christmas/Diwali/Holi/Rakhi/Raksha Bandhan/Eid/New Year node exists anywhere in real navigation. The only occasion-shaped nav item is Gifting > Shop By Occasion > 'Festive' (generic, not tied to one named holiday -- excluded, see below). Cross-checked sitemap-categories.xml (5726 /c/ URLs) and sitemap-otherpages.xml for any dedicated seasonal hub; none found outside main nav. However the sitemap surfaced ~130 poetically-named '/c/<slug>' marketing collection pages using holiday words (diwali-carnival, diwali-divinity, ready-for-diwali, christmas-cheer, christmas-home-decor, whiffs-of-christmas, holi-hues, holi-home, a-delightful-holi, the-rakhi-edit, rakhi-revelries, mystic-rakhis, gifts-rakhis-for-rakshabandhan, for-a-mubarak-eid, eid-elegance, this-mothers-day-say-it-with-a-saree, fathers-day-special, navratri-red, karwachauth-edit, brass-ganesha-idols, makar-sankranti-2025, etc.) -- none of these are reachable from the real nav (breadcrumb on every one reads 'Home > Collections > <name>', a generic orphan bucket, vs. genuine taxonomy pages which breadcrumb as 'Home > Gifting > Shop By Occasion > ...'). Verified a nonsense slug (/c/asdkjqwoieuqwoeiuxyz123) 404s cleanly, so these are real registered pages, not universally-faked ones -- each was individually content-sampled (title + rendered product grid, several with deep scroll for 100-200+ products) rather than judged by name/qty alone, per the false-positive check required for this task. Result: every single one of these holiday-named collections turned out to be a generic catalog reused under a festive URL, EXCEPT one: 'Diwali Carnival' (8) and 'Diwali Divinity' (8) are literally the same 6 products (copper/brass candle stands and jars) under two different names -- the exact duplicate-product-ID red flag called out in the task; both empty/expired: Whiffs Of Christmas, Rakhi Revelries, Mystic Rakhis (0 products each, dead campaign pages still resolving); 'Christmas Home Decor' (508 products, deep-scrolled ~300) = coffee sets, urli, bar tools, cutlery, plates, cushion covers, roti box, thali set -- zero Christmas iconography (no tree/ornament/wreath/stocking/Santa); 'Christmas Cheer' (56) = cheese boards, trays, bowls, tea-light holders, planters, same generic pattern; 'Holi Hues' (543) = entirely women's brass jewelry (earrings/necklaces/bangles), nothing color/Holi-specific; 'Holi Home' (226) and 'A Delightful Holi' (9) = generic tableware/tray/cake-stand; 'The Rakhi Edit' (358, deep-scrolled ~250) = generic men's shirts, kurtas, women's jewelry and dupattas, zero rakhi threads; 'For A Mubarak Eid' (72) and 'Eid Elegance' (196) = generic lighting/curtains/plates/jewelry/shirts, no Eid-specific items; 'This Mothers Day Say It With A Saree' (55) = plain sarees (any saree, not a Mother's-Day-specific product type); 'Fathers Day Special' (12) = generic bar tools/bowls/coffee sets/candles; 'Ready For Diwali' (38, deep-scrolled in full) = potli bags, heels, sarees, silver jewelry -- no diyas/candles/rangoli/lanterns, nothing Diwali-specific; 'Navratri Red' (133) and 'Karwachauth Edit' (209) = generic lehenga/kurta/dupatta filtered by color, not occasion-specific; 'Makar Sankranti 2025' (114) = generic jewelry; 'Brass Ganesha Idol' (104) = the year-round Idols & Puja Essentials catalog filtered to material=Brass + deity=Ganesha, not a Ganesh Chaturthi campaign. The ONE genuine exception: 'Gifts & Rakhis For Rakshabandhan' (419 products, breadcrumb Home > Collections > Gifts & Rakhis For Rakshabandhan) -- deep-scrolled ~190 of 419 products and every single one is an actual rakhi thread/bracelet or lumba (companion bracelet) from named artisan brands (Aumbray, Juhi Malhotra, Sangeeta Boochra Jaipur, Kicky & Perky, Abhika Creations, Arte Jewels) -- these ARE the literal ritual object tied for Raksha Bandhan, not a repurposed generic catalog, so this one passes the content-verification test and is included despite not appearing in main nav (rules allow a genuine 'Collection' PLP with its own grid/qty even when it's not in the mega menu). Also checked and excluded per shared rules: main-nav 'Diyas' (Home > Lighting > Diyas, 105 products) -- a normal year-round lighting product-type category, not labeled Diwali by the site (product-type != seasonal category, rule 5). 'Festive' (Gifting > Shop By Occasion > Festive, gifts-for-festivels, 1246 products) -- genuine real-nav occasion node but generic/ambiguous: sits alongside Wedding/Birthday & Anniversary/Farewell as a personal-occasion filter, not tied to one named holiday, and its sample products (coffee sets, glasses, cheese boards, a few idols/festive lighting) show no consistent single-holiday character -- flagged as the explicit Diwali/Festive ambiguity case called out in the rules and excluded rather than assumed to be Diwali; logged to qa_notes.md for adjudication. Also excluded as generic non-occasion-specific reused catalogs: 'Shop By Occasion' root (1882 products) and 'Jaypore Utsav' (Collections > Jaypore Utsav, 4931 products, all women's jewelry) -- both far too broad/generic to be any single holiday. No genuine Christmas, Diwali-decor, Holi, Eid, New Year, Navratri, Ganesh Chaturthi, Karwa Chauth, Makar Sankranti, Mother's Day, or Father's Day PLP exists on this site; the sole surviving row is Raksha Bandhan.

rows.evidence: Page header 'Gifts & Rakhis for Rakshabandhan - 419 products'; deep-scroll sample of ~190 products confirmed 100% genuine rakhi threads/bracelets and lumbas from named artisan brands (Aumbray, Juhi Malhotra, Sangeeta Boochra Jaipur, Kicky & Perky, Abhika Creations, Arte Jewels) -- e.g. 'Multicolor Tie Up Brass Rakhi', 'Kids Cotton, Wood, Wool, Ceramic Rakhis & Lumbas', 'Red Tie Up 925 Sterling Silver Om Rakhi' -- no generic reused catalog items found in the sample.
